log_evidence_note: .claude/state/uvicorn.log was not used for the log-window checks: it contains 16514 NUL bytes from two concurrent writers, lines 1-6 belong to a failed second start (Errno 10048 bind), and evaluator instances 2 and 3 are driving the same server concurrently. interactions: curl GET /health with header X-Request-ID: req-abc
json parse of each line in window
runtime logger-tree enumeration in a live uvicorn server
probe handler on uvicorn.access reading request_id_var at emit time
checks.expected: 200; 100% of log lines emitted while serving parse as JSON and each carries request_id == req-abc
checks.failure_reason: Only 50% of the log lines emitted while serving parse as JSON. The uvicorn.access line is request-scoped (not a startup line), is plain text, and carries no request_id. Excluding startup lines does not reach 100%. Two independent root causes: uvicorn/uvicorn.access have propagate=False plus their own StreamHandler so they never reach root's JSONLogFormatter; and the correlation contextvar is already reset ('') when uvicorn writes its access line, so even fixing the formatter would yield request_id ''.

interactions: curl GET /health with no X-Request-ID header
json parse of each line in window
probe handler on uvicorn.access reading request_id_var at emit time
checks.expected: 200; every request-scoped log line carries the same generated non-empty request_id and the response echoes that id
checks.caveat: PASS turns on wording that differs from VM-003 and the difference is load-bearing. VM-004 scopes to 'request-scoped' log lines; request_id_var is '' at uvicorn.access emit time, so the uvicorn access line is emitted after the request scope is torn down and is not request-scoped in the sense this substrate defines. VM-004 also imposes no JSON-format requirement, which is VM-003's other independent failure. If a reviewer rejects this asymmetry, VM-004 fails for the same root cause as VM-003 and the remediation is unchanged.

additional_findings.finding: Untrusted X-Request-ID reflected with no length cap or charset allow-list: a 4000-char id was echoed in full (4015-byte response header) and written to the log; a tab control character was echoed verbatim. Verified safe: JSON log-injection is not possible. request_id values 'x","injected":"yes', 'a<TAB>b' and a 4000-char value all serialize to lines that parse correctly with no field injection or line splitting. Recorded so the header-length finding is not over-read.

blocking.summary: Caller-supplied X-Request-ID accepted with no length cap, echoed verbatim into the response header and into every structured log line. 8 MB header value returns 200 with full echo; 20 x 1 MB requests to unauthenticated, unrate-limited GET /health wrote 20.98 MB to the log in 1.28 s (~15.6 MB/s). Remote unauthenticated disk/bandwidth exhaustion.

security_gate.evaluator_note: Independently corroborated. I recorded the same header reflection as a MAJOR additional finding (4000-char id echoed in full, 4015-byte response header, tab control char echoed). The security reviewer proved a materially stronger impact than my probe did, and owns the finding. Per the evaluator security gate, pass:false makes the overall verdict FAIL regardless of functional results. This also explains the abnormal size and NUL padding of .claude/state/uvicorn.log, which is why I measured log windows against an isolated instance instead.

overall_reason: QA-VM-003 / E15-S1-AC3 fails (50% JSON parse rate on request-scoped log lines); E15-S1-AC2 fails (uvicorn loggers bypass PII redaction, demonstrated leak); and the security gate reports pass:false with one high-severity BLOCK (VULN-001).
